body.p: Claims 1-2 and 4-9 are pending in the present application. Claims 1-2 and 4-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §101. Claims 1-2 and 4-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) as being indefinite. Claims 1-2 and 4-9 appear to be rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2020/0094845 to Shiga in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2020/0292322 to Ozog. Reconsideration of this application is respectfully requested in view of remarks and amendments submitted herewith.

The undersigned thanks Examiner Nguyen for the telephonic interview of February 11, 2025. The claims of the subject application were discussed in view of the 35 U.S.C. §112(b) rejection, the 35 U.S.C. §101 rejection, and the 35 U.S.C. §103 rejection. A tentative agreement was reached regarding proposed amendments, which are formally presented herein, to overcome the 35 U.S.C. §112(b) and the 35 U.S.C. §101 rejections. However, no agreement was reached regarding the 35 U.S.C. §103 rejection. However, the Examiner indicated that an updated search and consideration would be required.
Entry of this statement of substance of interview is requested as this statement is in compliance with 37 C.F.R. §1.133.

Applicant respectfully requests that claims 1, 7, and 8 be amended and that claim 9 be canceled. Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, figures, and claims as originally filed. It is believed that no new matter has been entered through these amendments and entry is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-2 and 4-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §101 as being directed to an abstract idea without significantly more. The rejection is respectfully traversed.
As tentatively agreed during the interview, Applicant respectfully submits that the amendments to independent claims 1, 7, and 8 satisfy the requirements of 35 U.S.C. §101.
Withdrawal of the rejection and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested.
Claims 1-2 and 4-8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112(b) as being indefinite. The rejection is respectfully traversed.
As tentatively agreed during the interview, Applicant respectfully submits that the amendments to independent claims 1, 7, and 8 satisfy the requirements of 35 U.S.C. §112(b).
Withdrawal of the rejection and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested.
Claims 1-2 and 4-9 appear to be rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Shiga in view of Ozog. The rejection is respectfully traversed.

The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. KSR, 550 U.S. at 416, 82 USPQ2d at 1395; Sakraida v. AG Pro, Inc., 425 U.S. 273, 282, 189 USPQ 449, 453 (1976); Anderson's-Black Rock, Inc. v. Pavement Salvage Co., 396 U.S. 57, 62- 63, 163 USPQ 673, 675 (1969); Great Atl. & P. Tea Co. v. Supermarket Equip. Corp., 340 U.S. 147, 152, 87 USPQ 303, 306 (1950). Further, "a prior art reference must be considered in its entirety, i.e., as a whole, including portions that would lead away from the claimed invention." W.L. Gore & Assoc., Inc. v. Garlock, Inc., 721 F.2d 1540, 220 USPQ 303 (Fed. Cir. 1983), cert. denied, 469 U.S. 851 (1984).

Applicant respectfully submits that Shiga in view of Ozog fails to disclose or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1. Specifically, Shiga in view of Ozog fails to disclose or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1 regarding acquiring, via the one or more

sensors, driving environment information and driving state information related to the autonomous driving, including an occurrence of rapid acceleration or deceleration of the autonomous driving vehicle to determine a vehicle control state, a driving route undertaken by the autonomous driving vehicle, and a driving position of the autonomous driving vehicle when the vehicle control state becomes a particular state that includes rapid steering or evacuation driving or the rapid acceleration or deceleration, and as similarly amended in independent claims
7 and 8.

The Office relies on paragraphs [0057]-[0060] of Shiga as disclosing or suggesting acquiring driving environment information related to the autonomous driving, including an occurrence of rapid acceleration or deceleration of the autonomous driving vehicle to determine a vehicle control state, becomes a particular state that includes rapid steering or evacuation driving or the rapid acceleration or deceleration (Office Action at p. 8). Paragraphs [0057]-[0060] of Shiga disclose displaying, on a touch display, a query to a passenger at a predetermined time prior to an expected arrive time when the vehicle is expected to arrive at a destination of the passenger. However, such disclosure does not reasonably disclose or suggest acquiring, via the one or more sensors, driving environment information and driving state information related to the autonomous driving, including an occurrence of rapid acceleration or deceleration of the autonomous driving vehicle to determine a vehicle control state, a driving route undertaken by the autonomous driving vehicle, and a driving position of the autonomous driving vehicle when the vehicle control state becomes a particular state that includes rapid steering or evacuation driving or the rapid acceleration or deceleration, as recited in amended independent claims 1, 7, and 8.

Shiga in view of Ozog further fails to disclose or suggest the features of amended independent claim 1 regarding determining one or more request questions for requesting an answer from the passenger from among one or more managed questions based on the driving environment information and the driving state information and in accordance with the vehicle control state, and as similarly amended in independent claims 7 and 8.

The Office relies on paragraphs [0057]-[0058] of Shiga as disclosing or suggesting determining one or more request questions for requesting an answer from the passenger from among one or more managed questions (Office Action at p. As previously mentioned above,

paragraphs [0057]-[0058] of Shiga disclose displaying, on a touch display, a query to a passenger at a predetermined time prior to an expected arrive time when the vehicle is expected to arrive at a destination of the passenger. However, such disclosure does not reasonably disclose or suggest determining one or more request questions for requesting an answer from the passenger from among one or more managed questions based on the driving environment information and the driving state information and in accordance with the vehicle control state, as further recited in amended independent claims 1, 7, and 8.

Based on the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1, 7, and 8, and all claims that depend therefrom, can no longer be rejected as being unpatentable over Shiga in view of Ozog. Further, Ozog fails to cure the deficiencies of Shiga.
Withdrawal of the rejection and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response. Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.

The fee under 37 CFR §1.17(e)(1) for filing a Request for Continued Examination is being submitted contemporaneously with the filing of this paper. No additional fees are believed to be due. However, the Director is hereby authorized to charge all required fees (including any extension of time fees) and to credit any overpayment of fees in this and any concurrent or future correspondence to Deposit Account No. 041133.
